about: The games played for vibration with a DualSense or DualSense Edge on a Mac. A game is added after a session, from what was felt and what the Wine modules logged, never from what it should do. Each test names its controller and its connection. docs/vibration.md is made from this file by tools/vibration-md.py.
stack: MacGameFix's Wine modules in a NotProton runner (CrossOver Preview 27), Steam Input off for the game, unless a result says otherwise.

results.not-recorded: Played; how it felt was not recorded

games.name: Marvel's Spider-Man 2
games.technology: Its own DualSense support, over raw HID. It plays its haptics as audio on the pad's audio output, which it finds by the audio endpoint's container.
games.description: Insomniac's PC port drives the pad itself, as on a PS5: haptics on the actuators and adaptive triggers, on a cable and over Bluetooth.
games.settings: Suggested: full motor power on the Edge and the Edge's haptics at 2x, on a cable and over Bluetooth.
details: It claims the motor power at 0x00 in every report for a standard DualSense, never for an Edge, which keeps its own stored reduction. With the power at full and the haptics at 2x the Edge felt like a standard DualSense.
It sends the same haptic signal to both pads (a level meter showed the same peaks and RMS for the same moments).
It reads feature reports 0x09, 0x20 and 0x05 only.
The touchpad moved the in-game camera (2026-10-20).

tests.notes: The same as on a cable.
The same as on a cable at 1x.

games.name: F1 23

games.description: Codemasters' game uses Sony's own library for the pad: haptics and trigger effects on a cable and over Bluetooth, with the Edge shown as a standard DualSense.
games.settings: Suggested: the Edge shown as a standard DualSense, and a DualSense's haptics at 2x over Bluetooth. Steam Input off: with it on, the haptics over Bluetooth started and stopped.
details: Under NotProton, as an Edge, the game assigned no buttons ("No preset control scheme", 2026-10-15).
The level meter showed the same continuous signal leaving the modules with Steam Input on or off.

tests.notes: In a CrossOver Preview bottle, seen as an Edge: buttons, haptics and triggers.
Jerky at 1x, steady at 2x.

games.technology: Not analysed. It plays haptics as audio and sends motor values beside them.
games.description: Its haptics came with the action over Bluetooth once the modules stopped writing copies of its motor reports.
details: It sends motor values all the time beside its haptics, up to about 18 control reports a second. Over Bluetooth those copies took the room the haptics need, and the haptics restarted 54 times in two minutes, until the modules stopped writing a copy while haptics stream.

tests.notes: The haptics output was open: the game asked for 32 ms of buffer.
The queue held 29 ms on average and 34 at most; 94 haptics reports every 2 s, nothing dropped.

games.name: Mortal Kombat 1
games.technology: SDL 2 (SDL2.dll 2.32.0), which drives the pad over HID: the rumble as the pad's emulation of motors.
games.description: Each rumble ends with its hit, on a cable and over Bluetooth, since the Wine modules of 2026-10-20.
games.settings: Rumble on the haptic actuators is optional over Bluetooth.
details: SDL 2 asks an Edge (firmware 0x0217) for the old emulation at half strength and a DualSense from firmware 2.24 for the improved one at full; the modules give the Edge the improved one at twice what SDL wrote, as SDL 3 would.
SDL ends a rumble with a report that has no rumble bit; over Bluetooth the modules missed it until 2026-10-20, and the rumble went on for the whole fight.

tests.notes: 17 rumbles in 74 s, the motors on 6 % of the time, each ended by SDL's stop.
15 rumbles in 38 s, about 250 ms each.
34 rumbles in 73 s, none longer than 239 ms.

games.settings: The pad as an XInput controller (by the store's rule). Trigger effects for the game from Game Feel: R2 slope, and resist while L2 is pressed.

tests.notes: 82 rumbles in 218 s, 154 ms each at the median. Rumble on the haptic actuators felt right too.

games.name: Resident Evil Requiem
games.technology: Capcom's RE Engine, with Sony's pad library linked in, over raw HID. It chooses between its own audio vibration device, when it believes the pad's audio output exists, and the motors, and it tells Bluetooth from a cable.
games.description: Over Bluetooth it vibrates with Bluetooth as a cable turned off for the game: it then sees a Bluetooth pad with no audio output and vibrates it itself. With the pad shown as wired it sets the trigger effects, never opens the pad's audio output and leaves the motors at zero.
games.settings: Game Feel: Bluetooth as a cable off for this game.
details: With Bluetooth as a cable on (the default), the modules logged trigger effects and motor values always at 0, and no haptics output opened (2026-10-21).
It vibrated the same way on NotProton's direct mode, without an audio output (2026-10-16).
Not played on a cable with the modules yet.

tests.notes: Bluetooth as a cable off for the game.

games.name: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Splintered Fate
games.technology: Super Evil Megacorp's engine. It reads the pad through XInput and through a path of its own, where it shows a DualSense.
games.description: As an XInput controller it vibrates, but the game sees the controller twice. With XInput off it sees one controller, shown as a DualSense, and does not vibrate.
games.settings: Game Feel: XInput off for this game, against the duplicate.
details: With the pad as an XInput controller the modules logged the game rumbling it through XInput.
Next: XInput's rumble on the motors alone (the defaults), so the game keeps its own DualSense and rumbles through XInput.

tests.notes: As an XInput controller: vibration, and the controller twice. XInput off: one controller, no vibration.

games.name: Nioh 3
games.technology: Its own DualSense support, over raw HID. It looks for the pad's audio output through SetupAPI: it reads the pad's container (SPDRP_BASE_CONTAINERID) and searches the audio render interfaces for the same one.
games.description: The game finds the pad and sets its lights and triggers, but never vibrates. With two SetupAPI patches of the modules (0009 and 0010, not released) it finds the pad's audio output, asks for its path and stops searching, but never opens it.
games.settings: In the game: all five vibration options on, mode Immersive.
details: Without patch 0009 it asked for the audio render interfaces about 70 times a second and got an empty list every time.
With 0009 and 0010 it finds the output whose container is the pad's, asks for its path once and stops; it never opens it, as audio, through MMDevice or as a file.
It writes the old rumble emulation once, with both motors at 0, and never a motor value after that; its pad thread sets XInput's vibration to 0 every frame.
It creates and releases XAudio2 without ever playing through it.
Neither the Edge shown as a DualSense nor XInput off for the game changed it.
Proton on Linux shows the same: the triggers work and the haptic vibration does not (ValveSoftware/Proton#9473).

games.name: Mortal Kombat 11
games.technology: NetherRealm's engine (the PC port by QLOC). It reads the pad through DirectInput with its own table, which has the DualSense's id (054C:0CE6) and not the Edge's; the Sony library it ships (2017) knows neither pad.
games.description: With XInput off and the Edge shown as a DualSense it plays with the right controls and PlayStation prompts ("never played so well"), but it does not vibrate. With the pad also given as an XInput controller (the store's rule) the buttons were assigned wrong.
games.settings: Game Feel: the Edge shown as a DualSense; XInput off, on the motors or as a controller gives the same. Steam Input off.
details: No motor value and no XInput vibration in the modules' log, in either session.

Its executable sends its rumble to XInput (XInputSetState) or to Sony's library (scePadSetVibration), and creates no DirectInput force-feedback effect. The Sony library it ships (2017) does not open a DualSense, and with the pad read through DirectInput the game wrote nothing to XInput, even with the pad there as an XInput controller too.

tests.notes: XInput off, with Steam Input still on for the game. Controls and PlayStation prompts right.
XInput's rumble on the motors, Steam Input off: no vibration request reached the modules in 3 minutes.
The pad also as an XInput controller, Steam Input off: still no vibration request.
